topic: The 1% fee: what a fund's expense ratio costs over 30 years

slides.title:
Your fund's
1% fee isn't
**small.**
slides.sub: It never shows up as a bill. Here's what it costs.

slides.title:
You never **pay** it.
It's just gone.
slides.body: A fund's running cost (the **expense ratio**) comes out of the fund itself, a little every day. Your statement shows what's left, not the charge.

slides.title: What 1% a year costs over **30 years.**
slides.body:
$10,000 growing 7% a year ≈ $76,123.
Same money, minus a 1% yearly fee ≈ $57,435.
slides.source: Illustrative maths, not a forecast: steady 7% vs 6% a year, compounded yearly.

slides.title: On-chain, every fee sits on a **public record.**
slides.body: Every holding, trade and fee can be checked by you, any time. The catch: prices swing more and the tech is newer. Start small.

slides.title: Look up your fund's **expense ratio** today.
slides.body: It takes two minutes, and many index funds charge far less. Follow BLOK Capital for plain-English money lessons.
slides.disclaimer: Educational content only, not financial or investment advice. On-chain assets can be volatile and you can lose money.
